note: Clean pass with two disclosed caveats. SOURCE / STEP 3b: Powell PA, PLOS ONE 13(3):e0194569 (CC BY 4.0). The live table is the study's own S1 Dataset (s005) columns QCAE1..QCAE31, 1-4 Likert, n=523 pooled over Experiments 1+2 -- the paper's Measures section states '31 items ... 4-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 4 = strongly agree)', 19 cognitive and 12 affective, which matches the live data exactly, so the table name, dictionary Description and content agree. MAPPING: data/powell_2018_empathy.py melts the source columns unchanged (var_name='item'), so the IRW code IS the source column name -- no positional or renaming step. The deposit carries NO item wording, however: the S2 File (Dataset variable definitions) says only 'QCAE# | QCAE questionnaire item # | Ordinal | 1-4'. That sentence is what ties each code to the instrument's own item NUMBER; the WORDS were then keyed by number to the canonical QCAE (Reniers RLEP, Corcoran R, Drake R, Shryane NM, Vollm BA (2011) J Pers Assess 93(1):84-95). For 27 of the 31 items the wording is verbatim from the numbered SPSS variable labels of an independent QCAE deposit -- Gomez R et al. (2022) PLOS ONE 17(1):e0261914, S2 File .sav (e.g. QCAE15 = '15. I can easily tell if someone else wants to enter a conversation.'), leading numbering stripped, nothing else altered; for the four reverse-worded items 1, 2, 17 and 29, which carry no label in that .sav, it is the canonical wording as shipped for gomez_2022_qcae in batch_041. So text_source is canonical_instrument, not study_materials: none of the wording comes from Powell's own materials. STEP 5b (PARTIAL, see verify_powell_2018_qcae.R): (a) summing the LIVE items under Reniers' subscale membership and reversing exactly items 1, 2, 17 and 29 reproduces the deposit's own CE and AE totals for 523 of 523 respondents, max |diff| = 0 -- arithmetic proof of which 19 items are Cognitive Empathy, which 12 Affective, and which four are reverse-worded; (b) the live table stores RAW (unreversed) responses -- the source file's separate rQCAE1/2/17/29 columns equal 5 minus their QCAE twin and are dropped by the build -- confirmed by item-rest correlations: QCAE1 = -0.398 against the rest of Online Simulation (the single reverse OS item) and QCAE11 = -0.521 against the rest of Peripheral Responsivity (the single FORWARD item in an otherwise reverse-worded block); (c) the per-item mean profile matches the independently label-tied Gomez sample at r = 0.921 over all 31 items, max |diff| 0.196, with the identity assignment fitting better than 99.9% of random within-subscale permutations for PT, OS and PRO. NOT ESTABLISHED: within-subscale order is not uniquely pinned -- near-tied items (e.g. PT 19 vs 27, EC and PER internally) leave some permutations competitive, so status is PARTIAL and within-subscale identity rests on the item numbering itself. ANCHORS: the live values are raw, so all 31 items get the same ascending anchors and none are flipped (unlike gomez_2022_qcae, whose four 'r' columns are stored already reversed). Powell states only the endpoints ('1 = strongly disagree, 4 = strongly agree'); the two middle labels, 'Slightly Disagree' and 'Slightly Agree', are the canonical QCAE anchors and are exactly the value labels the Gomez .sav carries for the same 1-4 coding, so they are transcribed from there rather than invented. instructions and section_prompt are blank -- neither the paper nor its supplements publishes participant-facing QCAE instructions (S1 File holds only the economic-game instructions), and nothing was invented. correct_response blank (attitude scale). RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register.csv carries no QCAE row, and the batch_041 sweep for the same instrument located no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause from Reniers et al.; the only restrictive sentence found there was Taylor & Francis's per-article PDF boilerplate, which governs that article file, not the instrument, and no wording here was copied from it. Silence is permission, so this ships.
public_note: Item wording for this table is not from Powell et al.'s own materials -- the deposit publishes only the item numbers ('QCAE# = QCAE questionnaire item #'). The text is the canonical QCAE keyed by that number, taken verbatim from the numbered SPSS variable labels of an independent QCAE deposit (Gomez et al. 2022) for 27 items and from the published instrument for the four reverse-worded items 1, 2, 17 and 29. The number-to-subscale mapping checks out exactly (the deposit's own cognitive and affective empathy totals reproduce for all 523 respondents), but order within a subscale rests on the item numbering rather than on anything in the data.
